title: sales-partnership-acme-media-notes-draft
content:
Account: Acme Media

Quick context:
- Digital publisher (news + niche verticals), ~120M monthly uniques, headquartered in NYC.
- Tech org ~200 engs, small data science/ML org (6-8). Recently announced personalization initiative + scale up of native ads.
- Current stack: internal microservices, AWS (EKS), using OpenAI for some content generation but heavy cost and occasional hallucinations reported in internal slack (link to convo in PS-342).

Why this matters:
- Acme likely cares about: latency & cost for high-volume generation, data security for ad content and PII, ability to run models on private infra for compliance with ad partners.
- Their personalization roadmap suggests they will need embeddings + real-time generation at scale - good fit for Redwood Dedicated or Private.

Key stakeholders (mapping):
- VP Eng: Maria Chen (decision maker on infra + vendor contracts)
- Head of Product: Lucas Rivera (owns personalization roadmap)
- Lead ML Engineer: Priya S. (hands-on, will evaluate dev experience + metrics)
- Security/Legal: Helen Park (data privacy + contractual terms)

Recent signals:
- Job postings for 'ML infra engineer' (2 reqs) - hiring for scale.
- Small pilot using OpenAI in 'content-gen' microservice (sig costs). Slack thread mentions 'timeouts during peak'.
- Mention in interview: 'need consistent latency at scale' - pain point.

Top objections expected + quick rebuttals (scratchy):
- 'We already use OpenAI / vendor X; switching costly' -> Response: Not asking to rip+replace. Start with canary routes: use Redwood hosted API for low lift, then move high-volume routes to Dedicated for cost predictability; migrations can be incremental using same API surface.
- 'Cost concerns / unknown unit economics' -> Response: Redwood Optimize recommendations + per-route token level cost breakdown will show math. Offer a sample TCO model: map their 3 top-gen endpoints -> estimate tokens/day -> show Dedicated vs hosted.
- 'Latency/SLAs for personalization' -> Response: Dedicated capacity + KV/prefix caching + latency SLOs and fallbacks to smaller variants. We have benchmarks for 2-4x reduction vs naive serving (link in Confluence).
- 'Security / data residency' -> Response: Private deployments (VPC + on-prem options) + KMS/HSM + audit logs; can sign appropriate DPA and SOC2 addendum.

Outbound email drafts (A/B test):
1) Short intro (cold):
Subject: Cut LLM inference costs for Acme's personalization
Hi Lucas,
Quick note - saw Acme's personalization push and the OpenAI pilot. We help teams reduce per-request latency and token cost while keeping model quality consistent. Can I share a short TCO + latency sketch for one of your personalization endpoints? 10-15 min.
- Aisha

2) Personalized (long):
Subject: Helping Acme scale personalization (pilot -> Dedicated)
Hi Lucas / Maria,
Congrats on the personalization initiative. From what I can tell you're piloting gen models for article suggestions and native ad copy. Common issues we see: spikes in latency during traffic peaks, high per-token spend on top traffic pages, and concerns about ad-related data in 3rd-party APIs.
We've worked with publishers to run a hybrid rollout: small hosted API for experimentation, Dedicated reserved capacity for top routes, and a private deployment for sensitive ad processing. The outcome: 30-50% lower token spend on heavy routes, predictable latency, and simplified compliance. Happy to share a 2-slide sketch + 15-min call to see if it's relevant.
Best,
Aisha

Call script bullets (1st discovery):
- Quick intros (30s)
- 'Tell me about where gen models are in your stack' (pilot? prod?)
- Probe: top endpoints, average tokens per request, peak RPS, SLOs for latency
- Probe: cost visibility today? Who owns it? Any internal dashboards? (OpEx focus)
- Security question: Is any PII or ad partner data sent to third-party APIs?
- UX: How do you currently test model quality and regression? (need eval hooks)
- Close: propose 15-min follow-up + offer to run a cost/latency sketch for 1 endpoint

Quick pricing framing for internal use (high level):
- Hosted: fastest onboarding, per-token pricing
- Dedicated: monthly committed capacity, best for steady heavy routes (predictable OPEX)
- Private: upfront infra + license, for regulated / sensitive data

Open items / TODOs:
- Build TCO sketch for 'article-suggest' endpoint (ask Priya for sample token profiles).    [action: email Priya asking for 7-day token histogram + p50/p95 latency]
- Ask Noah for recent customer benchmark deck and shared slides (CONFLUENCE-1589). [action: Noah]
- Draft follow-up email template for warm intro from Lucas -> Maria targeting VP-level cost/ops concerns.
- Prep compliance one-pager for Helen Park (short list of controls + SOC2/DPA bullets)

Next steps (immediate):
- Reach out to Lucas via LinkedIn with short variant A (today)
- If no reply in 4 days, send personalized variant B and include a 2-slide sketch
- If positive response -> schedule 15-min discovery, collect token profile before call

Notes to self:
- Keep outreach light, emphasize predictable cost + latency SLOs
- Use customer story: 'Publisher X reduced peak spend by ~40% moving top 5 routes to Dedicated' (get exact numbers from Noah)
- Avoid heavy infra talk in first email; focus on measurable outcomes (cost, latency, compliance)

End of notes.
